page: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 2048.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 32.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage consists of a 1900 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and the network interface supports a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core CPU capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 61947.26 and a PassMark CPU score of 56826.42. Single-core performance is average, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1688.0. Memory bandwidth tests show average read-only large block speeds of 153.34 GB/sec and write large block speeds of 61.06 GB/sec. The instance demonstrates strong performance in database operations, scoring 26144.88 in PassMark database tests, and achieves an average of 55.61 million operations per second in Redis SET operations.

The x2iedn.16xlarge offers high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it a specialized option for memory-bound workloads. While multi-threaded and database benchmarks are strong, single-core CPU performance remains average, indicating that workloads requiring high single-thread clock speeds may not fully leverage this hardware profile. The inclusion of 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 50 Gbps network bandwidth provides balanced I/O capabilities, though the lack of dedicated GPU hardware limits its utility for heavy parallel computing tasks.

This instance is configured for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise applications, memory-intensive data processing, and caching layers. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio and strong multi-core performance also support software compilation and database operations.
